title: Grafik, Art Direction & Retail Design
intro: Bevor ich in die IT gewechselt bin, habe ich über 25 Jahre als Grafik-Designer und Art Director gearbeitet – für Marken, Agenturen und den Einzelhandel in Warschau und Berlin. Eine Auswahl dieser Arbeiten.

projects.title: Zalando Outlets – KIDS Department
projects.text:
Zalando Outlets KIDS Department

Creative Idea, project management, 3D modeling, illustration, print preparation, technical supervision; Kaiserstraße 90, Karlsruhe; Prager Str. 8, Dresden; 2023/24

As part of the design process for the opening of new stores in Karlsruhe and Dresden, I had the exciting task of creating, managing and implementing new design concepts at the Zalando in Karlsruhe and Dresden.

The goal? To create a standout shop-in-shop space that would attract parents' attention without feeling too disconnected from the rest of the outlet. It also needed to be easily replicable in other locations. The inspiration came from the beautiful German forests with their lush greenery and wildlife. I went for a minimalist, transformed Scandinavian style - think clean lines, natural materials and neutral colors, with a pop of one of Zalando's key colors to tie it all together.

To make the magic happen, I sketched out tree and animal silhouettes, then turned them into digital files for CNC routers. The silhouettes were cut from pine plywood and finished with a clear varnish for that natural touch. It was amazing to see the space come to life, with the forest-inspired design creating a fun, inviting atmosphere that both kids and parents loved. Picture: © Fotografie-Schepp

The whole process was a fantastic blend of creativity and technical know-how. From sketching initial concepts to overseeing the final installation, every step was a chance to bring something unique and engaging to the outlet experience. The end result was a KIDS department that not only looked great but also felt like a natural extension of the Zalando brand—a space that truly stood out while fitting seamlessly into the broader outlet environment. Picture: © Fotografie-Schepp

projects.title: Zalando Outlet Hamburg
projects.text:
Zalando Outlet Hamburg Fasssadendesign

Idee, Projektmanagement, 3D-Modeling, Adobe Illustrator, Druckvorbereitung, Fachaufsicht; Große Bleichen 19, 20354 Hamburg; 2022 / 2024

Der Store befindet sich im Herzen der Hamburger Altstadt. Nur 10 Gehminuten vom Hauptbahnhof entfernt, liegt es in der Nähe des Jungfernstiegs zwischen einer Einkaufsstraße und einem Kanal. Die kreative Herausforderung für die Außenwerbung bestand darin, dass das Outlet über zwei Eingänge verfügt, die gestalterisch teilweise getrennt betrachtet werden mussten. Foto: © Gregor Schuster

Der Haupteingang liegt an der schmalen Ladenstraße, daher is die Fassade ist nur aus der Nähe gut sichtbar. Bei der Gestaltung musste ich mich daher auf Augenhöhe konzentrieren… Foto: ©  Jasper Ehrich

… und um die Sichtbarkeit nach innen zu gewährleisten und gleichzeitig eine starke Wirkung nach außen zu erzielen, entschied ich mich für das Zalando-Logo, das als Fensterfolie aus Logoraster über zwei Schaufenstern angebracht wurde.

Im Gegensatz dazu öffnet sich die Fassade mit dem anderen Eingang großzügig den Passanten und ist in ihrer ganzen Pracht nur von den angrenzenden Brücken aus zu sehen. Da der Eingang über die schmalen Stege auf der Rückseite der Alten Post am Bleichenfleet zu erreichen ist, eignet sich die Fassade eigentlich nur für die Fernsicht.

Die Fassade konnte ich in diesem Fall großzügig gestalten, aber natürlich im Einklang mit der Haupteingangsfassade. Deshalb habe ich mich auch hier für das Zalando-Logo entschieden, und habe die Fensterfolie über die gesamte Höhe des Schaufensters eingeplant.

Für die Ausführung war die Werbetechnikfirma B-Branded zuständig, die meinen Entwurf professionell und hervorragend umgesetzt hat.

projects.title: Zalando Outlet Frankfurt am Main
projects.text:
Zalando Outlet Frankfurt Wall branding

Creative Idea, project management, 3D modeling, illustration, print preparation, technical supervision; Zeil 119, 60313 Frankfurt; 2023

At the very beginning of August '23 Zalando opened the new store in Frankfurt am Main, located on the bustling Zeil 119, presenting a striking and inviting storefront that effectively captures the attention of passersby. The façade design, characterized by a bold and minimalist approach, was used by me to emphasize Zalando's brand identity while simultaneously maintaining a clear view into the interior. Picture: © VALUES. Real Estate Holding GmbH

I created this cross section to provide insight into the floor plan and to show how different areas and departments are connected. It helped stakeholders in the design process understand the spatial organization of the store and how customers could move through the different shopping areas, and it set the stage for the overall wayfinding system in the store. Through this design element, I wanted to emphasize the importance of efficient circulation and clear wayfinding for a positive shopping experience. The over 15 meter high staircase wall enhances the overall flow and accessibility of the store, making it easier for customers to navigate between levels.

A clear and concise signage system I created is strategically placed throughout the store to provide information about different sections and levels. For the main way finding placement, I chose the wall, which is a touchpoint in the main customer journey, leading one way to the escalator and the other way to the elevator. This solution continues in the same location on each floor, making navigation easier and improving the overall customer experience.

As usual I refered to the landmarks by creating the icons for the department's wallpapers. This pattern adds a touch of sophistication and elegance, while also highlighting the city's rich history and architectural heritage. The contrast between the dark blue background and the white silhouettes creates a strong visual impact, drawing the eye to the wall and enhancing the overall ambiance of the store. By incorporating this unique design feature, the Zalando Outlet Frankfurt am Main not only showcases its commitment to local culture but also provides a memorable shopping experience for its customers. Foto: © Jasper Ehrich

In designing the storefront, I chose a prominent logo-shaped graphic that draws attention to the store's key selling points, such as discounts and product offerings. This dynamic element adds visual interest and reinforces the store's value proposition. By keeping the store windows relatively open, I created space for additional marketing implementations, such as posters or window stickers.

projects.title: Zalando Outlet Bielefeld
projects.text:
Zalando Outlet Bielefeld Storefront Signage / Wall Branding

Creative Idea, project management, 3D modeling, illustration, print preparation, technical supervision; Bahnhofstraße 33, 33602 Bielefeld; 2023

In the last days of summer 2023, Zalando opened the new store in Bielefeld, one of the three new stores in Germany that year, along with the one in Frankfurt am Main and one in Karlsruhe. In the first phase of designing the store in Bielefeld, I contributed to a new look for the façade and, of course, the outdoor advertising elements.

A solution was needed that would be eye-catching without obscuring the interior. At the same time, it should highlight the product range so that people would know what to expect. I proposed a number of different approaches in order to find out which material solutions would best suit the Zalando style and at the same time fit in with the local architecture.

To enliven the façade and create a suitable contour for the logo, I used anodized aluminium panels with an additional brushed texture. This allowed us to highlight our location without hiding the interior from the curious gaze of customers. The logo now stands out well against the background of the façade and, when backlit, looks great after dark.

I had to reduce the size of the logo due to the city's approval process for the façade signage. The last step was the design of the storefront, for which I used a design that had already been tested for the Cologne store. The picture shows the final facade in Bielefeld. Foto: © Jasper Ehrich Fotografie

projects.title: Zalando Outlet Köln II
projects.text:
Zalando Outlet Köln Storefront Signage / Wall Branding

Idea, project management, 3D modeling, illustration, print preparation, technical supervision; Schildergasse 70, 50667 Cologne; 2022

The Zalando Outlet in the old town of Cologne was the first outlet I designed and brought to the final stage of opening in my career at Zalando Outlets. The store is located on the main shopping street, so the surroundings are overloaded with a variety of cantilever signs. Due to the fact that the façade is relatively high, which could affect the window as not enough comes out, the challenge was to look for creative ideas to make the window more eye-catching.

To emphasize the brand and still keep the view into the store clear, I decided to combine the storefront design idea with the highlight wall in the entrance area.

The central point of the mall is highlighted by a massive open escalator staircase. This over 10m high wall was a great opportunity to showcase the brand and tie the entire outlet space together.

To cover the entire wall of the staircase I created a pattern made of Zalando logos. The whole wallpaper was produced in long banners and glued to the wall from the lifting platform.

To highlight the character of the elevator walls, I created several icons based on local landmarks and points of interest. The silhouettes were used to create neon lights and, by their very nature, indicate the floor levels.

To be consistent, I created seamless departmental patterns for the women's, men's, and design departments based on the icons used for the elevator walls. These were used to create high quality vinyl wallpaper and implemented on each floor.

projects.title: Zalando Outlet Berlin
projects.text:
Zalando Outlet Berlin Wall Branding

Idee, Projektmanagement, 3D-Modeling, Adobe Illustrator, Druckvorbereitung, Fachaufsicht; Tauentzienstraße 18, 10789 Berlin; 2022

After the first post-pandemic opening of the flagship store in the heart of West Berlin, next to the Berlin Zoo, I was faced with the task of branding the entrance area.

The task was to make the brand visible to pedestrians at eye level and to position the store on the market map of the city. I decided to place the Zalando logo on the map of Berlin in such a way that the centre of the logo points to the actual location on the map, surrounded by local landmarks and points of interest.

The typical toe shoe shaped Zalando logo is made of 10mm thick translucent orange acrylic glass, mounted on spacers to enhance the 3-dimensionality by casting a slight orange shadow. The map was printed on wall foil and glued directly to the wall. The implementation: Hruby Werbetechnik from Berlin.

projects.title: Zalando Beauty Station Berlin
projects.text:
Zalando Beauty Station Store Window Design

Creative Idea, project management, 3D modeling, illustration, print preparation, technical supervision; Weinmeisterstraße 2, 10178 Berlin; 2022

At the end of July 2018, Zalando's first beauty station opened a few steps away from Alexanderplatz in Berlin. In addition to presenting its range in its physical stores, Zalando also wants to get closer to its customers.

One of my first tasks after joining the Zalando Outlets team was to redesign the shop window and the cantilever signs. Due to the relatively limited visibility from the street and the fact that the window is open to pedestrians, I decided to place the logo on the window.

I designed a 3D shaped logo and placed it directly on the glass of the window. In this way I achieved a visual attraction without obstructing the view into the shop. The 3D logo is visible from the side view along the street as well as from the other side of the street. The implementation: Hruby Werbetechnik.

projects.title: Welcome to the Labyrinth
projects.text:
Welcome to the Labyrinth „Untitled“, Peter Kogler

3D modeling, Adobe Illustrator, pre-press, technical oversight; Marta, Museum für Kunst, Architektur, Design , Herford .

In 2018, I had the pleasure of collaborating with Peter Kogler, whose famous works are exhibited around the world. The task was to create a texture for one of Frank Gehry's deconstructionist exhibition spaces.

The space I had to work with was so non-geometric that I had to create a 3D model of the structure to understand what kind of surface I was working with. On the finished 3D model, I textured with graphics I received from the artist. I used this to create a vector artwork in Adobe Illustrator and used it for pre-press. I divided the whole texture into 18 individual surfaces and sent it to the plotter on several hundred square meters of special expandable self-adhesive film.

While working on site in Herford, I supervised the application of the foil to the walls, ceilings and floors. I was surprised by the complexity and difficulty of the task. At the time, it was one of my most complex jobs at the interface of graphic design and architecture.

PKO BP Corporate Leasing campaign

Idee, Art direction, Logo design; Poland; 2018

The PKO Bank Polski campaign was aimed at people - mostly from rural areas - who wanted to start their own business adventure - and it was a huge success!

The idea was that you can create something incredible from almost nothing. All you need is a good idea and support from the bank, and the sky is the limit! The shooting took place at the Alpaka farm near Warsaw. I have contributed to the idea, logo, script, press and online campaign.
